traits.label: Hymenium
traits.text: Tubular or poroid, with yellow to olive pores.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Hymenium: Tubular or poroid, with yellow to olive pores.

traits.label: Cap
traits.text: 5-12 cm in diameter. Convex to flat, slimy when wet, and shiny when dry. The cap is typically yellow to olive-brown.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Cap: 5-12 cm in diameter. Convex to flat, slimy when wet, and shiny when dry. The cap is typically yellow to olive-brown.

traits.label: Hymenium Attachment
traits.text: Adnate to slightly decurrent.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Hymenium Attachment: Adnate to slightly decurrent.

traits.label: Stipe
traits.text: Cylindrical, sometimes swollen at the base, yellow with a reddish-brown scabers towards the base.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Stipe: Cylindrical, sometimes swollen at the base, yellow with a reddish-brown scabers towards the base.

traits.label: Description
traits.text: Brown.
traits.raw: 🟤 Brown.

traits.label: Ecology
traits.text: Mycorrhizal, predominantly found in association with Aleppo pine trees, particularly in sandy soils.
traits.raw: 🌲 Mycorrhizal, predominantly found in association with Aleppo pine trees, particularly in sandy soils.

traits.label: Edibility
traits.text: Edible, but the slimy cap skin should be removed before consumption.
traits.raw: 🍲 Edible, but the slimy cap skin should be removed before consumption.

traits.label: Fruit body
traits.text: Up to 10 cm tall.
traits.raw: 📏 Up to 10 cm tall.

traits.label: Microscopy
traits.text: Spores are elliptical, smooth, 8-10 x 3-4 µm.
traits.raw: 🔬 Spores are elliptical, smooth, 8-10 x 3-4 µm.

traits.label: Odour
traits.text: Mild or not distinctive.
traits.raw: 👃 Mild or not distinctive.

traits.text: Known for its sticky cap and reddish-brown scabers on the lower stipe and its association with pines in sandy soils are key identification features.
